title: legal redlines scratchpad - samuel cole
content:
Quick scratchpad for reviewing vendor/customer contract redlines. Mostly notes to self + suggested fallback language. Rough, unpolished.

Context:
- Draft is a standard customer MSA + SOW for Dedicated deployment (GPU-reserved) with a healthcare customer. Sensitive PHI possibility; need to ensure Private deployment/KMS options are explicitly available. See JIRA-9876 for deal thread.
- Key ask from sales: push for minimal changes to pricing + keep SLA 99.9% w/ credits. Customer pushing for higher liability cap and broader data use rights.

Clauses to watch (high priority):
1) Data usage / Model training prohibition
   - Customer requests ability to use output for "product improvement". Red flag: could be interpreted as training our models.
   - Suggested counter: "Vendor shall not use Customer Data or Customer Outputs to train models used in production without Customer's prior written consent". Add exceptions for aggregated/anonymous telemetry strictly limited to service operation (e.g. telemetry for performance/availability).
   - Ask: Sales to confirm whether customer expects embeddings to be retained for search indexing. If yes, need explicit retention/custodian terms.

2) Indemnification / IP carveouts
   - Customer wants broad indemnity for third-party claims related to outputs. Need to limit: indemnity for IP only where output directly infringes and Vendor provided the prompt templates or model.
   - Counter language: indemnity limited to direct infringement claims caused by Vendor-delivered models or pre-packaged content; exclude customer prompts.

3) Liability cap & consequential damages
   - Customer pushing for unlimited liability for data breach. Unacceptable.
   - Standard: cap at the greater of (a) fees paid in prior 12 months or (b) $XM (negotiation point). Keep consequential damages excluded except for breach of confidentiality and willful misconduct.

4) Data security / PHI handling / audit rights
   - If PHI plausible, we MUST ensure: BAA signed, encryption at rest/in transit, KMS/HSM options, logging and access controls.
   - Audit rights: customer requests on-site audits. Prefer SOC2 report + right to audit via third-party with notice rather than full on-site.
   - Suggested: "Vendor will maintain SOC2 Type II and provide report upon reasonable request; on-site audits permitted only with 60 days' notice and at Customer expense, limited to once per 12 months."

5) Subprocessors & private deployments
   - Customer wants no subprocessors without consent. For Dedicated/Private we should allow specified cloud vendors/partners but require notification and veto for new sensitive subprocessors.
   - For Private (on-prem/VPC), ensure we include statement that customer data remains within customer-managed network when Private option chosen.

6) SLA / Credits / Remedies
   - Customer pushing for immediate termination rights for missed SLAs. Prefer cure period + tiered credits.
   - Suggested: 99.9% monthly uptime SLO with credits schedule; termination allowed only after 3 consecutive months below threshold and failure to cure within 30 days.

7) Termination / Data return & deletion
   - Need clear retention and deletion obligations: timeline for returning/deleting customer data, confirmation of deletion, exception for backups and legal holds.

8) Confidentiality / residuals
   - Customer asks to prohibit residual use. We should accept standard residuals language (unauthorized retention of unstructured memory not deliberate).

9) Export controls & sanctions
   - Ensure we have right to refuse service for sanctioned entities and comply with export laws. Customer may request guarantee; keep vendor right to comply with applicable laws.

10) Support & maintenance / security patching SLA
   - Define support hours, severity definitions, response and resolution targets. Make sure patching of underlying model/runtime doesn't create unacceptable downtime; add maintenance windows + notice for disruptive upgrades.

Negotiation talking points (what Sales should emphasize):
- Product differentiation: our Dedicated/Private option mitigates data residency & PHI concerns — KMS integration + on-prem option reduces their risk.
- SOC2 + pen test cadence: we provide SOC2 reports and can run tailored assessments under NDA (limited scope).
- Telemetry: explain aggregated telemetry is minimal and only used for performance; offer to carve out PII/PHI from telemetry.
- Liability: emphasize shared risk; our pricing and commitments reflect operational investment.

Suggested fallback language / redline snippets (quick):
- Data training prohibition: "Vendor shall not use Customer Data or Customer Outputs to train, improve or benchmark models for use beyond the Customer's own tenant, without Customer's prior written consent."
- Liability cap: "Except for liability resulting from breach of confidentiality or willful misconduct, Vendor's liability shall be limited to the greater of (i) fees paid under the Order Form in the twelve (12) months preceding the event giving rise to the claim, or (ii) $2,000,000." (figure TBD)
- Audit: "Vendor shall provide SOC2 Type II reports. On-site audits require 60 days' notice and are subject to mutually acceptable scope and confidentiality protections; Customer shall bear reasonable costs."
- SLA termination: "Customer may terminate for material breach only if Vendor fails to cure within 30 days after written notice and the service has failed to meet the uptime SLA for three (3) consecutive months."

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide $ cap (work with finance/risk). Quick proxy: start negotiation at $2M, floor $500k for SMB deals.
- Confirm with infra whether we can support selective telemetry blocking (PII/PHI) per customer.
- Confirm BAA process timeline with compliance.
- Review SOW deliverables: acceptance criteria for model tuning, bench tests, and performance baselines. Add objective metrics where possible (p50/p95 latency, tokens/s throughput).

Notes to self:
- Keep redlines short and prescriptive. Avoid vague "reasonable" obligations where possible.
- For healthcare vertical, default to Private deployment unless customer insists otherwise — it's a negotiation lever (cost vs. security).
- Keep track of precedent language in internal contracts repo (see github PR link).

Conversation snippets to include in reply to customer (sales enable):
- "We absolutely do not train on customer data without consent. We can, however, provide aggregated telemetry that excludes PII/PHI and is used solely to maintain service reliability."
- "For auditability, we provide SOC2 Type II reports and will work with you on a targeted third-party assessment if needed under an NDA."
- "Termination for SLA failures is a last resort — we provide tiered credits and a cure period to protect both parties and avoid service disruption."

Last checks before sending redlines to customer-facing repo:
- Confirm liability cap number with GC/Finance.
- Ensure we include fallback for Private option and explicit KMS/HSM language if customer requires key control.
- Add short appendix in SOW listing model versions allowed for deployment and expected maintenance windows.

---
Rough, keep refining. Will pull precedent clauses from contracts repo (PR #42) and update.

Samuel
